Enzym.et:
Coined by German physiologist Wilhelm Friedrich Kühne in 1878.
From Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + ζύμη (zúmē, “sourdough”).

s: encyclopedia (comprehensive reference work with articles on a wide range of topics)
Enzyklopädie.et: Variant of earlier Encyclopädie, from New Latin encyclopaedia with influence from French encyclopédie, from Koine Greek ἐγκύκλιος παιδείᾱ (enkúklios paideíā, “education in the circle of arts and sciences”), from Ancient Greek ἐγκύκλιος (enkúklios, “circular”) …

enzyklopädisch.et: Probably borrowed from French encyclopédique. By surface analysis, Enzyklopädie + -isch.

Enzian.et: From Old High German encian, variant of genciane, from Latin gentiana.
